verdict.reasoning: REFUTED on four independent grounds. (1) NOTHING IS MISSING. The heading is present, verbatim and complete, at specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 24038 as '## 14.6.9.4 Space filling a dynamic table', preceded by a correct anchor '' at line 24037. The clause number and title match the PDF exactly; the body paragraph beneath it matches too. The kind 'missing-heading' is factually wrong - no PDF text was lost. (2) THE PDF ENCODES NO HEADING LEVEL AT ALL, so there is nothing for the transcription to have dropped. I extracted the span metrics from specs/'ISO_COBOL_2023.pdf' with PyMuPDF: PDF pages 574 and 575 contain exactly ONE bold style between them, Cambria,Bold at 11.67pt (145 and 131 chars respectively), used for every heading. The 300-dpi renders confirm it visually: on page 574 (printed 544) the parent '14.6.9 Operations on dynamic-capacity tables' and its children '14.6.9.1 General', '14.6.9.2 Moving a table', '14.6.9.3 Comparing two tables' are all set in identical bold face and size - even parent and child are typographically indistinguishable; on page 575 (printed 545) '14.6.9.4 Space filling a dynamic table', '14.6.10 Overlapping operands' and '14.6.11 Normal run unit termination' are likewise identical. ISO uses one uniform heading style for all clause depths here, so the '###' vs '##' distinction exists only in the markdown and is unverifiable against the source. (3) THE CLAIM MISQUOTES BOTH SOURCES. The 'pdf_says' field attributes a markdown heading level to the PDF, which the PDF does not express, and its own sentence says the heading is rendered at '###' when the transcription renders it at '##' (the '###' items are the siblings). The line number is wrong: the heading is at line 24038, not 24035. (4) THE '#' DEPTH IS GLOBALLY NON-SEMANTIC IN THIS TRANSCRIPTION, so no convention is uniquely violated here. Across the whole file, four-part clause numbers (x.y.z.w) are written 620x as '###', 162x as '##', 24x as '####'; three-part numbers 508x '###', 276x '##', 17x '####'; two-part numbers 162x '##', 26x '###'. Identical 'anomalies' surround the flagged one in the very same section: 14.6 is '##' and so is its child 14.6.9; 14.6.1 is '###' but its sibling 14.6.2 is '##'; 14.6.2.3.1 is '####' while its siblings 14.6.2.3.2 and 14.6.2.3.3 are '##'; 14.6.2.4 is '##' while siblings 14.6.2.1-.3 are '###'; 14.6.13.1.2 and 14.6.13.1.3 are '##' while siblings 14.6.13.1.4-.1.6 are '###'. (An additional look-ahead duplicate block at lines 24099-24107, before the '' marker, is flattened to '##' throughout while the canonical page-576 copy at 24142-24148 uses '##'/'###'/'####' - the same noise again.) (5) NO MEANING CHANGES. The hierarchy is carried by the printed clause number '14.6.9.4' and by the anchor id 'section-14-6-9-4', both correct. Cross-references resolve by number and anchor, not by '#' count - including the reference on page 574 itself, 'as specified in 14.6.9.4, Space filling a dynamic table', which lands correctly. The claim's stated harm ('appears to close out 14.6.9 and open a new peer section') does not even follow, since the parent 14.6.9 is itself at '##'. This is a document-wide markdown formatting characteristic, not a page-575 content discrepancy between the PDF and its transcription.
